objective: Run an instrumented, end-to-end proof of concept of the real Rhino CAD MCP workflow through the Git bridge, without improving or modifying the system during the run, so the resulting evidence reveals actual friction, missing capabilities, failure modes, and opportunities to make the bridge smoother.
instructions: This is a baseline observation run, not a fix/build task. Do not modify bridge/runtime/control-plane implementation while executing the POC. Record kinks instead of fixing them.
Use the rhino-chatgpt-orientation Claude skill first in operator mode and apply the fresh canonical payload silently.

From /Users/nes/bin/mcp/rhino-cad-mcp on a clean, up-to-date main, use the normal manual Claude operator lifecycle: fetch/pull --ff-only, discover this request, then ./exchange.sh prepare bridge-phase12-001.

Before touching Rhino, create .bridge/evidence/bridge-phase12-001/session-log.json with a chronological event log. For every major stage record UTC timestamp, stage name, outcome, elapsed_seconds when measurable, human_intervention_required, retries, and concise notes. Keep updating this evidence throughout the run.

Record baseline bridge/operator facts: orientation load result, local branch/base commit, Git status cleanliness, request discovery method, branch preparation result, Claude version if queryable, and whether the rhino-cad MCP server/tools are visible in the current Claude session.

Inventory the available rhino-cad MCP tool names relevant to this POC before using them. Compare actual availability against the capabilities described by README/CLAUDE.md. Record missing, renamed, duplicated, or unexpectedly unavailable tools as observations; do not modify code to reconcile them.

Run a non-mutating Rhino connectivity preflight using the available MCP interface. At minimum attempt the equivalent of rhino_status and document listing/inspection. Record the raw structured outcomes, target/document identifiers, round-trip timing if returned, and any ambiguity or retries.

Protect the user's existing Rhino work. The POC must use a dedicated new test document if the MCP exposes a safe create-document capability. Name it clearly for this run, for example RHINO_CHATGPT_BRIDGE_POC_001. If a safe dedicated-document path cannot be established, STOP before mutation and report that as a high-severity workflow blocker rather than modifying an existing user document.

In the isolated POC document, create a small but non-trivial three-solid assembly using deterministic RhinoCommon through the MCP: a rectangular base, a vertical cylindrical pedestal, and a smaller top block/cap. Use sensible dimensions in the document units and keep the objects separated/stacked intentionally so validation is interpretable.

Exercise semantic organization if the available MCP supports it: create/use a dedicated layer, assign object names or user-string metadata such as role, created_by, revision, and operation_id, and confirm the metadata by readback. If a high-level tool is absent, record that fact; do not add a new tool during this baseline run.

Validate each created object with the available object-inspection/validation surface. Record GUIDs, object type, validity, solidity/manifold status where applicable, bounding boxes, dimensions/volume if available, and metadata readback.
Run assembly-level validation if available, including solid validity and bounded interference/duplicate checks. If assembly validation is unavailable, record the missing capability explicitly.

Capture visual evidence using the available viewport capture or visual-QA tool. Prefer a deterministic isometric view plus at least one orthographic or secondary view if supported. Store controller-reviewable artifacts under .bridge/artifacts/bridge-phase12-001/ when practical. At minimum preserve the capture manifest and a PNG in that directory. If the MCP insists on another output path, copy only the resulting evidence artifacts into the bridge artifact directory without altering their contents.

Save the isolated POC document to a deterministic temporary/local artifact path using the verified save/save-as surface if available. Record save verification results, file size, object count, and readback status. Do not overwrite an existing file.

After geometry, validation, capture, and save, re-inspect the test document and record final object/layer counts and target identity. Do not close or delete the test document if doing so would risk losing evidence; clearly report its final state so the user can decide whether to keep or close it.

Create .bridge/evidence/bridge-phase12-001/workflow-assessment.json. It must include: architecture_path_observed, stage_metrics, mcp_tool_inventory, rhino_preflight, document_isolation, cad_operations, validation_results, artifact_manifest, save_results, retries_and_errors, manual_interventions, ambiguities, friction_points, and recommendations.

For friction_points, classify each issue with severity high/medium/low and category chosen from onboarding, git_bridge, request_protocol, branch_lifecycle, mcp_discovery, rhino_targeting, mutation_safety, tool_schema, latency_timeout, artifact_handoff, validation, reporting, or other. Include concrete evidence and the exact stage where it occurred.
For recommendations, separate QUICK_WINS from PROTOCOL_CHANGES from MCP_RUNTIME_CHANGES. Do not implement any recommendation in this task.

Also create .bridge/evidence/bridge-phase12-001/operator-experience.md as a concise narrative from the operator's perspective: what felt smooth, what was awkward, what required reasoning that should have been automated, what required manual intervention, and the top five workflow improvements ranked by impact. This is an observational ranking of workflow improvements, not a change to the system.

Measure the full workflow from orientation/start through pushed receipt. Include total elapsed time if possible and the count of Git commands, MCP calls, retries, user/manual interventions, and distinct handoff steps. Exact counts are preferred; label estimates as estimates.

Do not change server.py, bridge.py, runtime_ops.py, tool_support.py, snippets.py, test_bridge.py, requirements.txt, knowledge/, tests/, operator.sh, exchange.sh, orient.sh, .bridge/bridge_cli.py, orientation files, CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, or any skill/installer files during this baseline POC.

Do not install dependencies, edit MCP registrations, restart/reconfigure services unless the existing workflow absolutely cannot proceed without it. If a restart/reconfiguration is required, STOP and report it as a blocker rather than silently changing the environment.
Run git diff --check and verify the task branch contains only POC evidence/artifacts/report files, not implementation changes.
Commit all POC evidence/artifacts as the work commit and capture RESULT_COMMIT.

Create .bridge/reports/bridge-phase12-001.json using the v0.3 report schema with ack exactly BRIDGE-PHASE12-RHINO-POC-20260924-3B91D4-OPERATOR-ACK, exact base_commit, RESULT_COMMIT, and branch operator/bridge-phase12-001.

The report summary must state whether the full path ChatGPT controller -> Git request -> Claude operator -> rhino-cad MCP -> rhinocode/Rhino -> validation/artifacts -> Git report was demonstrated end to end, partially demonstrated, or blocked, and name the first failing stage if not complete.
Run python3 .bridge/bridge_cli.py verify-report bridge-phase12-001 and require REPORT_OK.
Commit the report as the separate receipt commit, push operator/bridge-phase12-001, and do not merge it.
expected_outputs: .bridge/artifacts/bridge-phase12-001/ containing at least a viewport PNG and capture/scene manifest when the Rhino path reaches visual evidence
constraints: Baseline observation only: do not fix or modify the bridge/MCP/runtime during the POC.
Never mutate an existing user Rhino document; require an isolated POC document before CAD mutation.
Do not invent unavailable tool results or claim Rhino validation that did not occur.
Do not overwrite existing files or artifacts.
No dependency installation, MCP reconfiguration, force push, or merge.
If a safety prerequisite fails, stop at that stage and capture the blocker as useful POC evidence.
